title: A Season of Stolen Tomorrows
subtitle: Campaign · Campaign framework · open consequences, not a fixed plot

fields.label: Campaign question
fields.value: Can Bellwether keep its life-saving wonders without allowing anyone to own another person's future?

fields.label: Arc 1 · Consent
fields.value: Begin with The Night Without Tomorrow. Follow the forged roll and decide what proof, people and infrastructure to preserve.

fields.label: Arc 2 · Dependence
fields.value: Explore who profits from lawful loans as well as fraud. Neighboring districts offer rival solutions; the Unwritten and Office can split, reform or cooperate according to play.

fields.label: Arc 3 · Ownership
fields.value: Confront the founding compact behind the tower. The future debt holder in Ira's trouble can emerge through player agreement; their identity and solution are not pre-scripted.

fields.label: Moving interests
fields.value: Vale seeks a legacy or escape; the rescue wing protects people; the purists target records; hospital staff need a functioning reserve. Advance plans only when the fiction and PCs' choices warrant it.

fields.label: Milestones
fields.value: Use Core milestones at appropriate fiction-driven points: minor opportunities to adjust a character, significant milestones for scenario/arc development, major milestones for major changes. Apply the actual advancement rules, not automatic rewards per session.

fields.label: Ending space
fields.value: A reformed utility, decentralized time commons, a city that abandons the tower, or a costly new compact are all possible. Let decisions establish the outcome.
